desert_p09_001.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_001.text: Yue carried the red flag to the edge of camp while Gao checked the northern sky. High pale cloud had begun gathering beyond the dark ridge, too thin to promise rain. The wind now came from the basin side instead of the west. Tuo listened to the lower rushing note, then asked the drivers to look at the visible return bend. They went together, taking no cart. The stove shield trembled but held. The house sounded urgent in a way a building could not intend. Yue tried to hear the change without letting its urgency become her own conclusion.

desert_p09_002.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p09_002.text: The old sign belongs beside a winter surge reading. We are in another season, and wind alone has several ways to make this shaft louder. I want the sky, the ground, and the channel checked before anyone calls it a flood warning. Keep the treatment area sheltered. Han, move the loose account sheets into their case. Du, give me the exact copied line instead of a summary from memory. Yue, stand where the returning drivers can see the flag. If they report a changed road, we shall use the report, not the house's excellent dramatic voice.

desert_p09_003.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_003.text: The drivers returned with dust on their boots and an ordinary answer. The gravel bend remained dry. They had seen no water across the wheel line, no fallen rock, and no damaged marker. Farther east a dark strip showed below the loading apron, but it might be old dampness in deeper shade. Gao marked a place to compare at dawn. Han asked whether they should leave immediately. Tuo looked toward the narrow descent, then the darkening sky. Driving it in failing light would add a hazard they could already name.

desert_p09_004.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_004.text: Preparing for the morning remained the stronger choice on the evidence they had. While the returning drivers gave their report, one brown mule shied at a sheet snapping from the cart shade. Long Legs had been brushing its shoulder with the lead held loosely. The animal pulled away before he could tighten his grip, circling toward the courtyard line. Tuo rose halfway from her chair and stopped when her ankle protested. She called the driver to the mule's familiar side instead of shouting at its head. The companion mule lifted its ears.

desert_p09_005.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_005.text: Yue moved the fallen cloth out of the path, giving the startled animal one less thing to face. The brown mule stopped short of the cord around the hollow slab, then backed toward the eating shade. Long Legs approached with his hands low and spoke the same quiet words he used at feeding. Yue stayed on firm gravel beside the open route to its companion. She did not try to grab a moving lead across the animal's legs. The mule turned toward the familiar pair and let the driver take the loop. The whole escape lasted less than a minute.

desert_p09_006.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_006.text: It left everyone breathing as though the animal had carried them farther than the day's walk.

desert_p09_007.speaker: tuo_yin
desert_p09_007.text: Tie that sheet before it gives us another demonstration. The mule did not invent a theory about the house; it heard cloth where cloth had been still. Long Legs, check the lead loop where it scraped the stone. Farrier, tell me whether that mark is only surface wear. Yue, keep the passage clear until both animals settle. Then somebody bring my chair back into its original place. I appear to have travelled half the courtyard without moving my foot, which is impressive but deeply inconvenient when the water table now stands between me and supper.

desert_p09_008.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_008.text: The farrier replaced the scuffed loop with a sound spare from his harness kit and kept the damaged piece for repair. Long Legs accepted the inspection without defending his grip. He had loosened it because brushing worked better when the animal could move its neck; the gust had arrived at the wrong moment. Gao secured the shade sheet with an extra tie taken from their issued bundle. Bao examined the driver's hands and found only a dusty scrape. Nobody required a villain to explain the incident. They did require a better fixed cloth before settling back to work.

desert_p09_009.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_009.text: Yue helped move Tuo's chair out of the altered traffic line. The guide was angry with herself for starting to stand, then more angry that the irritation had become obvious. Yue offered no lesson about following medical advice. She placed the water cup within reach and asked whether the chair faced the flag position clearly. Tuo looked, adjusted it a little, and said it did now. A useful question gave her something besides the ankle to govern. The brown mule rested its head near its sister. Its calm returned faster than the humans' offended sense of control.

desert_p09_010.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_010.text: The quiet driver told Yue the brown pair had always preferred standing together. She would rearrange their temporary leads so a cloth gust could not send one toward the hollow boundary again. The change shortened neither animal's ability to reach its water trough. She measured the new sweep with her boot and asked the farrier to watch before accepting it. Yue kept the shade edge raised while the knots were checked. Their work looked like an elaborate dance to a spectator who knew nothing of its purpose. From inside it, each movement answered a particular small fear.

desert_p09_011.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_011.text: Han arrived with the loose sheet folded beneath his arm. He asked whether it belonged to Gao's equipment or the common shade. The common shade, she said; its original tie had loosened when the wind changed direction. He put the damaged tie beside the spare-loop record and asked the camp worker what material would hold better for the next journey. The worker named a broader tape sold by the same outfitter in Bitter Wells. Han wrote it down. A purchase for the future did not repair the present wind, but it kept today's inconvenience from becoming next month's familiar one.

desert_p09_012.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_012.text: When Yue returned the flag to its waiting place, Long Legs thanked her for leaving him a clear route to the animal. She said Tuo had done the difficult part from a chair. He agreed, then asked that nobody tell his mother he had briefly lost the mule while explaining to people how carefully he watched it. Yue said she would report only what mattered. He looked relieved until she added that his mother's opinion might be relevant to future harness design. His laugh came back a little shaky. She waited beside him until the mule stopped rolling its eyes.

desert_p09_013.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_013.text: The cook asked the driver holding the fuel bag to stop looking at the ruin long enough to weigh the next portion. Their task had its own urgency, measured by the raw batch waiting in the casks. The first batches already credited to the tank had been cooled and measured properly. The rest still needed treatment. Bao checked the wind shield's position and kept the clean receiving vessel beneath its cover. Yue returned to the writing table after lowering the flag. She had spent much of the day waiting for useful findings.

desert_p09_014.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_014.text: Now useful work demanded that she remain with familiar details. A gust lifted one chalk card and carried it against the raw cask. The word cooled faced outward where it did not belong. Yue caught the card before somebody used the misleading label, then fastened all three with heavier ties. The cook watched her and said that a kitchen on wheels ought to hire its own wind clerk. She said the post sounded exhausting. He replied that it was, but offered unlimited complaints instead of a good salary. Bao told them to save their complaints until the last measured batch.

desert_p09_015.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_015.text: The joke ended where the clean transfer began. The next kettle reached its full boil. The cook held it for the agreed time, then lifted it toward the cooling block with a driver helping at the other handle. A sudden gust pushed grit across their faces. They stopped, but the driver's sleeve caught the folded cloth beneath his grip. The kettle tipped enough to spill a thin sheet of hot water onto empty gravel. Nobody was struck. The cook set it down, swore without ceremony, and asked Bao to check the driver's wrist. The skin remained unburned.

desert_p09_016.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_016.text: The lost volume would not return because they had avoided injury. Yue entered the spill after the kettle cooled enough to measure what remained. The driver tried to apologise three times. Bao accepted the first and redirected the rest toward changing the carrying cloth. Han fetched a broader dry pad from the stove box. They moved the cooling block closer so the next transfer would not require stepping through the strongest wind. The cook tested the new grip with an empty pot before continuing. Their adjustment was neither grand nor complete.

desert_p09_017.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_017.text: It removed the particular arrangement that had turned a small gust into a loss. Gao checked the treatment record against the fuel book. The measured pace remained within the reserved allowance, though the spill reduced the expected clean addition. Nobody altered the draw limit to make the final number look better. The cistern retained its agreed reserve. Han seemed tempted to ask for one more can, then looked at the dark path and let the thought end. Bao needed the crew rested for the return, not making another carrying trip to replace every imperfect litre.

desert_p09_018.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_018.text: Yue saw how easily a plan could become unreasonable by trying to preserve its beautiful original total. Tuo sat with her ankle raised and directed supper traffic around the treatment screen. One driver nearly stepped into the cooling corner while reaching for a bowl. She caught him with a sharp word and then pointed to the longer route. He obeyed, annoyed for two steps, grateful by the third. Her limited walking had made her notice the camp's small crossings more exactly than she usually did. She called it an unfortunate career advancement.

desert_p09_019.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_019.text: Bao said she would recommend retirement from the new post as soon as the ankle recovered. Du offered to design a commemorative map no customer would purchase. Supper arrived in portions while the water continued heating. The cook ate standing until Bao put a stool behind him with unmistakable intent. A driver took the fuel weighing for the next batch, and Gao watched its timing while Yue rested her writing hand. The meal included the longer-cooked stems set aside at lunch. They had softened into something pleasantly bitter.

desert_p09_020.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_020.text: Yue recognised her own little sorting task in the bowl and felt connected to the meal beyond receiving it. The crew's work kept appearing later in altered forms, sometimes as soup, sometimes as a road another person could use. Han read his daughter's letter again while the others ate. Her mother's cough had eased, but the note also mentioned a bill from the roof repairer and a creditor who preferred punctuality to charm. He folded the page before anyone could see the figures. Gao asked whether the business letter's threat would hurt them badly.

desert_p09_021.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_021.text: He said losing the larger subscribers' future freight would matter. He could still refuse to keep a dangerous route quiet. The refusal would not transform the loss into a pleasant thing. She nodded, appreciating an answer that did not pretend courage settled accounts at home.

desert_p09_022.speaker: han_xun
desert_p09_022.text: I used to imagine decent decisions would advertise themselves well enough that business followed naturally. Then I met several people with excellent principles and very empty warehouses. Sometimes you pay for what you decide. We should say that without making payment an argument against deciding. My daughter dislikes hearing me sound noble about it; she asks whether I have paid the shopkeeper first. Usually I have. Sometimes she has to remind me. The insurers may welcome a careful provisional report more than the subscribers fear. I hope so.

desert_p09_023.speaker: han_xun
desert_p09_023.text: Hope is allowed at the table, provided it does not sign the invoice.

desert_p09_024.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_024.text: Yue thought of the broken jar in Bitter Wells, paid for before Han knew she would work for him. His ordinary generosity had seemed easy then. The letter made its setting visible: a household, debts, a firm that depended on people who could resent being warned. She did not tell him the jar proved he would choose correctly forever. He might still make mistakes under pressure. She could respect him without turning one morning into a certificate of permanent goodness. The thought reminded her of Tuo's rebuke beside the hollow slab, and she found herself smiling at the lesson's return.

desert_p09_025.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_025.text: Later Long Legs approached Han about payment for the water carrying. He had not carried either cask himself, which made the request less awkward and more pointed. The quiet driver and farrier had accepted a heavy task beyond their ordinary cart turns. Han said the water served the whole crew. Long Legs agreed, then said shared benefit did not make every person's extra shoulders a free resource. Gao looked up from the treatment card. She disliked the timing but could not dismiss the point. Han set his family letter aside and asked the driver to name what he was requesting.

desert_p09_026.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_026.text: He asked for an extra half-day's work entered for the two hired carriers, separate from the waiting wage already owed. Gao and Han had carried too, but their compensation arrangements differed. The quiet driver stood nearby, embarrassed that someone spoke for her and unwilling to pretend the effort had cost nothing. She said she would have carried regardless because the return margin mattered. Long Legs answered that willingness was precisely why the work should not vanish from the account. The farrier said he preferred an ordinary entry to a generous speech. The request had become unexpectedly difficult to refuse honestly.

desert_p09_027.speaker: han_xun
desert_p09_027.text: You are right about the entry. I treated the task as an urgent part of providing our own return, and forgot that the heavy carrying fell on particular people. I can pay the additional half-day from the survey contingency account. It will reduce my firm's margin, not the deposited return fare. Gao's professional account will record her added field time separately; mine remains an owner's cost. Give me the work book. I shall enter the two carrying turns and show each person before we leave. Long Legs, your talent for noticing other people's inconvenience has improved since the bucket.

desert_p09_028.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_028.text: Long Legs bowed so deeply that the quiet driver threatened to use him as a table. The humour let her accept the entry without making gratitude her wage. Han wrote the extra work while the farrier checked the wording. Payment would be settled at the receiving house with the ordinary accounts, and the workers retained a copied entry. Nobody took coins from the green return purse. Yue saw a second form of finite resource become visible: effort, distributed less neatly than water between people whose contracts had been written before the ruined station made its request.

desert_p09_029.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_029.text: Gao thanked Long Legs for raising the matter after the immediate cask movement rather than during a difficult lift. He said he valued all his teeth, including the ones she might otherwise remove by expression alone. She smiled reluctantly. The quiet driver told him to stop collecting credit for being the crew's conscience. He said conscience paid badly and he would prefer a different post. Their laughter moved through the camp with less strain than the previous mule episode. Han returned the family letter to his coat, looking thoughtful rather than triumphant about accepting a correction.

desert_p09_030.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_030.text: Yue asked the quiet driver whether the new entry would matter much. The woman said half a day could pay for several weeks of oil in her mother's lamp. Her mother sewed after sunset and insisted the eyes were still perfectly sound. The driver carried supplies home that let the insistence remain comfortable. She would not have refused the cask job without the extra pay, but she liked Han better for recognising it. Yue thought of the family letters lying in separate packs.

desert_p09_031.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_031.text: The road's large accounts kept arriving as small objects in rooms nobody on the caravan could presently see. The farrier added his copy to the mule records rather than his money pouch. He said the work belonged beside the reason it had been done. Yue found that practical and slightly eccentric. He explained that a former employer once forgot an entire winter's extra hoof care while remembering every nail supplied. Since then he kept labour where the animals could metaphorically witness it. The metaphor remained a metaphor; Plum was occupied with chewing.

desert_p09_032.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_032.text: The little lesson made Yue laugh, and he looked pleased to have given advice without sounding like another teacher gathered around her notebook. Han did not ask the workers to withdraw the payment if the final report failed to sell a better route. The work had happened. Its value to them was not waiting for a subscriber's approval. That distinction gave Gao a thought for the source note: observations also happened before offices decided whether they were convenient. She wrote the sentence in rough form, then crossed it out because the report needed facts rather than a sermon.

desert_p09_033.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_033.text: Still, the idea remained in how she arranged the copied evidence. The people who supplied effort and knowledge would be named beside their actual contributions. Bao checked the carriers once more. Gao's earlier headache had eased, though her eyes tired when she read small figures. Han's palms needed a simple protective wrap for tomorrow's harness work. The driver's wrist remained sound after the hot spill. Their extra drinking portions stayed in the actual day column. Nobody's cup was reduced to compensate for the lost treatment water.

desert_p09_034.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_034.text: The distinction mattered: an accounting loss belonged in the record, while a thirsty person still required water. Yue had seen enough ledgers to know how often tidy totals could tempt people to reverse that order. The house changed its note again, lower now that the wind slackened. Du brought the copied level column to Gao without being asked. Its weather sign showed a basin wind followed by high channel water in midwinter. A separate mark indicated that staff closed the lower apron before the rise reached its outer edge.

desert_p09_035.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_035.text: The two entries described a sequence, not a mechanism that made any wind into a warning. Gao copied the sequence exactly. They would compare the visible dark strip at dawn and ask the quarry for current drainage work after returning. Neither task needed a prophecy. Gao's finger paused beside the tiny crooked wing in the margin. Du saw it this time. She asked where he learned that mark. He said his first field teacher used it for a reading requiring a return visit. The bird meant the observation should not be allowed to fly away from its unresolved condition.

desert_p09_036.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_036.text: Gao looked at the station copy, then at him. She had learned the same explanation from him years earlier. The similarity was inherited, not a signature that proved whose hand made every old note. Still, the old case had touched a part of his history he had not offered.

desert_p09_037.speaker: gao_ru
desert_p09_037.text: Did you work in this station group? I am asking because your source list names a retired record, while your account of the site has sounded entirely like reading from manuals and passing through with carriers. That wing may belong to anyone your teacher trained. I know that. But you recognised the column unusually quickly. If you have personal knowledge of how its restrictions were written, I want it beside the copied words. We have spent days asking other people which parts they witnessed. You should not be the exception merely because your books sit comfortably in our bags.

desert_p09_038.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_038.text: Du took off his spectacles and cleaned them longer than the lenses required. He had worked in the northern district's records office during the station group's closing years. He copied field returns, compared levels, and helped prepare public summaries. He did not operate the cistern or direct freight across the apron. His teacher inspected the lower exchange. The bird came from that school of work. He recognised the case type because several closing summaries had been transcribed from such columns. He had not known this case survived. Saying the facts plainly made his voice sound younger and less defended.

desert_p09_039.speaker: du_she
desert_p09_039.text: I left that office believing I would produce maps people could actually use. The old reports filled cupboards while carriers learned routes by asking a driver beside a trough. I made the sheets clearer, which helped. I also made some histories smaller, which did not always help. My public ridge line was sound when surveyed. The old station limits became a source note too short for the loading conditions inside it. I cannot tell you that omission caused today's fall.

desert_p09_040.speaker: du_she
desert_p09_040.text: I can tell you why the information was available to me and why my modern sheet made it hard to see.

desert_p09_041.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_041.text: Gao listened without offering a forgiving conclusion. Du had taught her to keep doubtful readings visible. His own published work had sometimes hidden their history under a clean route line. She knew the pressure: customers wanted distances, not pages of seasonal qualification. She had made her own compromises in field summaries. That made his admission harder to dismiss and harder to accept. Tuo watched from her chair. She said the carrier who dispatched her brother had also preferred a short instruction to a seasonal account. The roads differed. The habit of shortening could still be familiar.

desert_p09_042.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_042.text: Du asked whether Gao wanted him removed from the report. She said she wanted his source history included accurately, and the old record compared before he claimed anything about its authorship. Removal would not make the observations clearer. He nodded, visibly relieved and uncomfortable at once. Yue saw that consequence could be more demanding than banishment. He would continue working where the omission was visible, correcting the sheet beside people who now knew it. Han asked what disclosure belonged in the public source note.

desert_p09_043.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_043.text: Gao said office experience, source date, and the present copied limits, with no melodramatic confession in place of usable facts. After Du accepted the source disclosure, he told Gao about the records office in more detail. It occupied a cold room behind the northern receiving house. Young clerks copied field returns onto narrow sheets, each with a column for rejected or uncertain readings. His teacher insisted those columns survive the public summary. A senior official called them confusing and expensive to print. Some survived; others became a single sentence saying conditions varied by season.

desert_p09_044.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_044.text: Du learned how little ink an office required to turn a particular warning into general wisdom everybody could claim to have understood.

desert_p09_045.speaker: du_she
desert_p09_045.text: I wanted to leave because I thought useful maps could do better. They did in some ways. A carrier could find the public ridge without asking the loudest man at the trough. A village could appear by its own name rather than the nearest tax station. I am proud of that work. Pride then made me reluctant to show where clarity had cost detail. It is easier to defend a whole career than examine one shortened source note. You have asked me to do the latter. I should be grateful. At present gratitude is arriving with several less attractive companions.

desert_p09_046.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_046.text: Gao said she recognised those companions. In her first independent season she had omitted a doubtful afternoon reading because the morning set looked cleaner. The difference did not alter the final route, but an auditor noticed the missing observation sequence. She corrected it and spent a month angry at being caught in a small fault. Du had helped her prepare the response, telling her correction was stronger than a good excuse. She remembered that kindness now. His present omission did not cancel it. It made the advice something they both had to obey, especially when the road supplied inconvenient examples.

desert_p09_047.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_047.text: Du asked whether she had resented his advice at the time. Gao said profoundly, for about three days, then intermittently ever since. He laughed, relieved that the history could contain truth without becoming punishment alone. Tuo listened from the chair and said three days was an efficient apprenticeship in resentment. She preferred thorough practice. The familiar joke did not erase the source disclosure. It helped them keep discussing it without making every old kindness evidence for acquittal. Yue heard the distinction and thought it more difficult than the measurement tolerances written on Gao's instrument card.

desert_p09_048.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_048.text: Han asked whether the station office had retained the full reports elsewhere. Du thought the district archive received duplicate annual summaries, while local cases held the working columns. Some duplicates might have travelled north when the office closed. He would not promise their survival. The case before them could be one remaining source among several lost ones, which made copying it carefully worth a later commission. Gao asked for the receiving-house name and approximate dates he remembered. He supplied both, labelled as memory. The next enquiry had gained a starting place without pretending its answer already sat in the room.

desert_p09_049.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_049.text: Yue wanted to ask why Du had not said all this sooner. Gao asked first. He answered that he had regarded the office period as dull background to his real work. Passing the retired stations later, he wrote about wind and travellers because readers enjoyed those things. The narrow summaries, arguments over printed cautions, and his own compromises seemed like a cupboard he had left closed. He had not deliberately concealed a secret capable of explaining every present injury. He had underestimated the usefulness of an untidy part of his life. The answer sounded neither noble nor wholly evasive.

desert_p09_050.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_050.text: Gao said the cupboard had now opened, and they needed its useful papers more than its metaphor. Du agreed. He listed the distinctions between an annual level summary, a loading restriction, and a public route sheet on a clean page. Yue copied the headings beside the old column tracing. A water level did not become a ban unless somebody issued the restriction; a restriction did not become a safe reopening merely because another sheet omitted it. The relationships were complicated enough that Han asked for a concrete example. Du used the surviving winter entry rather than an invented accusation.

desert_p09_051.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_051.text: In that entry the level rose below the apron, an inspector advised closing heavy loads, and the office recorded closure two days later. A subsequent note reopened only the upper ridge. Their copy showed those words clearly. It did not show who sent any later freight consignment, or what repairs intervened. Han could present the record as a reason to inspect the current buried approach. He could not present it as proof that his rival's recent driver knowingly ignored a live ban. The subscribers might prefer a simpler accusation. Gao's report would give them a more useful question instead.

desert_p09_052.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_052.text: Tuo asked whether the old inspector's name survived. Du said the visible heading carried only office initials. A fuller register might identify the person, but their current view did not. She nodded. Her brother's enquiry had involved witnesses who wished to turn remembered phrases into names attached to blame. Some recollections helped; some grew more confident every time they were repeated. She did not want that habit carried into this report merely because the old record made a compelling shape. Du thanked her. For once the thanks did not require a joke to make it bearable.

desert_p09_053.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_053.text: The conversation ended with a task list rather than a verdict on Du. He would disclose the office experience, preserve the source dates and copied wording, and ask for the fuller record when they could return properly equipped. Gao would separate current observations from historical inference. Han would send the public route warning without patient details. Yue would keep the two-site figure legible. Tuo would contribute the local names and remembered paths. Bao would document the water treatment. Each person had something concrete to do. That was kinder than a sweeping absolution and more demanding than a dramatic condemnation.

desert_p09_054.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_054.text: The discussion ended because the cook called for the next measurement. Gao returned to the cooled vessel; Du put his spectacles on and copied the source note without abbreviating it. Yue held the lamp steady while he wrote. The tiny bird no longer looked like a secret code. It belonged to a practice passed from teacher to pupil, carrying a warning about unfinished work that every generation could still neglect. The mark had not accused him by itself. Their questions had required an answer from a living person, who could remember, explain, and take responsibility for what he actually did.

desert_p09_055.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_055.text: The last raw water passed through the filter. Bao inspected the cloth before the cook folded it for cleaning, keeping the retained sample sealed elsewhere. Both service casks were empty. Han marked them as borrowed equipment to return, not supplies consumed by the discovery. Their light weight would make tomorrow's loading easier. The quiet driver secured their lids for the journey. Yue watched the final kettle settle onto the stove and felt a weariness that belonged partly to anticipation ending. They had spent the day deciding whether the store could help.

desert_p09_056.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_056.text: Soon its help would be a measured number instead of a possibility. The cook used fourteen kilograms of charcoal for the complete treatment sequence. The tested stove arrangement and close lids kept it within the allowance despite the stronger wind. Cooking through supper had used thirteen kilograms in all since departure, leaving thirteen of the original forty for the return and contingency. He wrote the figures carefully, then handed the pencil to Yue because his fingers had begun to cramp. She copied them into the shared work page.

desert_p09_057.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_057.text: He said he would rather the report remembered the stove than his handwriting. She told him the handwriting had brought the stove's work home to the account. After every batch cooled and entered the tank by measured transfer, the total clean addition was one hundred and fifty-eight litres. Twelve of the one hundred and seventy raw litres had gone through evaporation and handling losses, including the spill. The inspection flushes and retained samples belonged to the separate twenty litres already drawn. Their measured cistern draw remained one hundred and ninety altogether.

desert_p09_058.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_058.text: Gao checked the addition against every batch entry, including those entered before the wind changed. The final total described the actual work; it did not add the first cooled kettle a second time. The day's caravan withdrawals totalled one hundred and seventy-four litres. Carriers had needed more drinking water than the initial forecast, while treatment and ordinary washing remained within their assigned portions. With the actual cistern addition, one thousand and sixty-one litres now stood in the tanks, protected compartment included. Han closed the water page after the drivers confirmed their tank depths.

desert_p09_059.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_059.text: The number gave the return a real margin. It did not promise another full day of scholarship. Gao repeated the morning departure, and Du agreed before anyone could ask whether the glass case might contain one more irresistible column. Tuo wanted the closing cistern note written plainly for future travellers. It would describe a roof store with about sixty accessible raw litres left by the checked gauge at their departure, subject to condition and later use. Foot access followed the northern ledge; the buried apron remained unsuitable for loaded carts. Water needed treatment before drinking.

desert_p09_060.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_060.text: Du drew the access large enough that a reader could see the dangerous shortcut beside it. Han said the note should go to the village collective and receiving house together. The people who knew the channel deserved the same current account as the offices selling distances. Yue folded the location copy and imagined the older guide reading it after recovering. He had waited beneath a broken cart within sight of a station whose water he did not know how to reach or trust.

desert_p09_061.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_061.text: A symbol could not have completed his rescue, but a better symbol might have changed his choices before the fall. She wanted the new sheet to be clear enough without pretending it could replace help. The wish was larger than one pencil. Gao gave her the final sketch to check, asking whether she could follow its approach using only what was drawn. Yue found one missing turn. They added the black outcrop and the north ledge's bend. Du thanked Yue instead of defending the simpler version. The correction took little time.

desert_p09_062.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_062.text: Its value would be known only if somebody later used it, which made it easy to undervalue now. Han put the public copy in a dry envelope. Tuo asked that the old local names remain beside the formal station labels. A map that renamed every known place could become accurate and unusable at the same time. Gao added the names carefully, keeping Crescent House and North Exchange separate rather than asking one familiar name to carry both buildings. Before loading preparations, Yue helped rinse the emptied service casks at the designated waste corner.

desert_p09_063.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_063.text: The rinse portion belonged to the day's actual washing allowance, and the casks remained marked for further cleaning and inspection by their owner on return. Han kept the loan slip with their identifiable issue marks. The keeper would not have to accept a vague claim that two barrels had been useful somewhere. Yue liked that practical end to an unusual day's work. An object could serve an important discovery and still require its ordinary return, with its lid, lining, and account intact.

desert_p09_064.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_064.text: The quiet driver checked Tuo's riding cushion again, placing it where road jolts would reach the body through padding rather than directly through the cart rail. Bao helped the guide enter once, slowly, then had her practise sitting with the foot supported. Tuo said everyone now knew more about her ankle than about the commission. Han promised to put it in the appendix if she insisted. She threatened to review his family letter for spelling. The driver laughed while keeping one hand at the brake. Tomorrow's return had acquired a passenger without losing its ordinary safeguards.

desert_p09_065.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_065.text: Yue laid the fish stone beside the packed notebook long enough to compare their sizes. Du noticed and said the ancient engineers would probably have measured its tail before deciding it was a fish. She told him the child would judge it more efficiently. He conceded that children had valuable methods unavailable to district offices. The little object had no relation to the water record, yet it made the return feel less abstract. Somewhere in Bitter Wells a girl had asked for a stone. Yue could bring it, and that small completed promise belonged beside the larger unfinished questions.

desert_p09_066.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_066.text: The driver with the wooden bird played his two notes after the last kettle moved off the stove. The house answered in a different interval, refusing the easy duet it had offered the previous evening. He said his daughter would appreciate a toy that had survived professional criticism. Tuo asked him to learn a third note before claiming a concert. He tried, produced a squeak, and looked offended at the wood. Yue laughed until her tired shoulders loosened. Their day had contained water, omissions, pay, and worry. The music was poor enough to give everyone a rest from competence.

desert_p09_067.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_067.text: Han wrote one more line to his daughter beneath the business account. He said the household picture now showed the correct number of wheels, but the drivers demanded flowers too. He did not mention the creditors to anyone else. Gao wrote to the cooperative secretary, enclosing the limited warning and the promised source disclosure. The two letters would leave together at the receiving house, then travel toward different kinds of concern. Yue had once imagined public work replaced private life during a journey. Here private life kept appearing in the way people chose their public words.

desert_p09_068.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_068.text: When the letters were put away, the camp worker collected the chalk cards and tied them inside the treatment box for another journey. Raw, heating, cooled: simple words that had mattered all afternoon. Yue helped brush grit from their edges. He said she could take credit for improving the ties if somebody later complained about his knots. She told him the knots had held after she stopped letting the wind choose their position. He accepted that division of blame cheerfully. The borrowed casks stood empty, the tanks held measured water, and the stove at last belonged only to tomorrow's breakfast.

desert_p09_069.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_069.text: When the stove finally cooled, camp grew quieter than it had all evening. The house continued a low intermittent rush. Bao checked Tuo's ankle, approved the morning riding arrangement, and sent everyone to sleep. Han lingered beside the second tank, resting his hand on its cool cover. Yue understood the gesture now: the stored water had become possible return, family letters, ordinary debts paid late rather than never. He caught her looking and lifted his hand, embarrassed. She said the joint beneath it was dry. He laughed softly and thanked her for giving him a practical reason to stand there.

desert_p09_070.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_070.text: Gao stayed at the lamp with Du's source note. He came to ask whether its wording was complete enough. She changed one line that made his old office role sound more distant than it was, then gave it back. He accepted the change. Their friendship would not settle tonight, but their report could become more accurate tonight. Yue saw the difference and left them to finish it. She packed her practice lead under the private notebook, untouched since the small supervised tests.

desert_p09_071.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_071.text: Stage five remained a stable part of the journey, while most of the day's useful work had required other kinds of courage. Before bed the quiet driver returned from one last look along the marked camp boundary. The return bend was still dry. Beneath the lower exchange's outer apron, however, the dark strip had widened since the earlier check; a bead of water stood on a pale seam that had held only dust in the morning. Gao went with her to observe from the sound ledge. They marked the present edge with a small chalk reference on exposed stone.

desert_p09_072.speaker: narrator
desert_p09_072.text: It was a real change, modest and unexplained. Tomorrow's closing look would compare it before the carts moved. Yue watched the chalk dry above the bead and felt the road acquiring another reason to speak carefully.
